content:
Working on cones, affine subspace, convex sets and polytopes I find myself reimplementing the same operations and lemmas over and over. I am talking about features inherited from sets, such as

  • ∅ and univ
  • singletons
  • Min and sInf
  • pointwise Neg
  • Zero and pointewise Add
  • pointewise VAdd (= Minkowski sum) and SMul
  • maps (i.e. type specific versions of image, range, preimage, ...)
  • ...

Since recently we have IsConcreteLE to indicate that the order relation on a SetLike object is essentially the same as on sets (see the thread here). And an IsConcreteSInf is on the way (#37446).

I would like to have the same for essentially all features of sets, that is, I would like to have various IsConcerete classes that carry over all essential functionality and lemmas. I played with this in the draft #39853 (CI complains because of missing doc-strings). There is also the more serious #38786 implementing IsConcreteNeg.

What do you think about this?

Implementing these classes is somewhat repetitive as I am essentially cloning the Set API with a proof that just applies the various IsConcrete-translations. Makes me wonder whether this could be automated to some degree by tagging Set-lemmas with some sort of @[setLike_concrete ...]. No detailed idea here.
I also wonder whether the current terminology could be improved: perhaps IsSetLikeLE, IsSetLikeNeg, IsSetLikeMin would be easier to recognize for what it is?

Sounds like this could be a good use case for a transport tactic.

#metaprogramming / tactics > transport tactic

But you said that your motivation is to reduce code duplication. Do you think we will still achieve that if we implement these IsConcrete classes manually?

Why do you need to write the same lemmas over and over? e.g. if you have a type of convex polytopes, and you define -x as {carrier := -x.carrier, ...}, then all of the basic lemmas about the negative of a convex polytope should reduce to a one-liner about the negative of sets.

Besides, as I said in that PR, you'll avoid a lot of duplication if you make use of the existing typeclasses on orders. Instead of proving a bunch of lemmas about the empty set as a convex set, you could just prove (⊥ : ConvexSet α).carrier = ∅ and now you can make use of all the lemmas you already had on ⊥.
This is essentially what we already do for stuff like Submonoid, Subgroup, Subring, ... and it's worked well enough so far.
tl;dr I'm skeptical that introducing more typeclasses is the best solution here.

Violeta Hernández said:

Why do you need to write the same lemmas over and over? e.g. if you have a type of convex polytopes, and you define -x as {carrier := -x.carrier, ...}, then all of the basic lemmas about the negative of a convex polytope should reduce to a one-liner about the negative of sets.

The point I think is to automate all these one-liner lemmas. So instead of writing the same one-liners on every set type with a Neg, you would put a single instance {α} : IsConcreteNeg (SubFoo α) where coe_neg _ := rfl and then you can use all the IsConcreteNeg lemmas and the same lemmas will be used for SubBars as well.

How many lemmas do we expect to be automated? Five? Ten? Fifty?

If we're introducing ten new typeclasses just to automate a couple of trivial lemmas then I don't think that's worth the churn.
If the proofs of these lemmas are all ext; simp then I also don't think it's worthwhile.

Violeta Hernández said:

If we're introducing ten new typeclasses just to automate a couple of trivial lemmas then I don't think that's worth the churn.

Fun fact: we recently got IsOneApply / IsOneApplyEqSelf / IsZeroApply / IsMulApply / IsMulApplyEqComp / IsAddApply / IsDivApply / IsSubApply / IsInvApply / IsNegApply / IsSMulApply / IsVAddApply / IsPowApply / IsNatCastApply / IsIntCastApply

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

But you said that your motivation is to reduce code duplication. Do you think we will still achieve that if we implement these IsConcrete classes manually?

Yes I think so. Even without meta programming, implementing these classes means duplicating once rather than dozens of times.

Violeta Hernández said:

How many lemmas do we expect to be automated? Five? Ten? Fifty?

Personally I am working with ~10 types that need this functionality (Submodule, AffineSubspace, PointedCone, ProperCone, PolyhedralCone, ConvexSet, Polytope, Polyhedron, ConvexBody, ...). But I guess every type of the algebraic hierarchy is a candidate. But it is also about the amount of lemmas that need duplications. It is on the order of ~100. I am not going to write all these ~1000 lemmas. I would write them once for the classes though.

I wonder whether you judge what I propose as somehow different from what IsConcreteLE already does?

And yes, the point is to automate mostly these one-liners. It is annoying to keep track of what coe-lemmas to apply: I need to coe equality, order, membership, ... and whatever feature the lemma I want to apply uses (see my PR). With the appropriate automation these become simps, while otherwise they cannot be simps because some simp-iff-s are applied backwards.

Violeta Hernández said:

Besides, as I said in that PR, you'll avoid a lot of duplication if you make use of the existing typeclasses on orders. Instead of proving a bunch of lemmas about the empty set as a convex set, you could just prove (⊥ : ConvexSet α).carrier = ∅ and now you can make use of all the lemmas you already had on ⊥.

I agree that I should have implemented IsConcreteBot instead of IsConcreteEmpty, assuming that appropriate delaborators will be provided. I was not aware of this at the time. Still, currently Set duplicates the order lemmas for ∅ and I am duplicating Set-API, so this is why I wrote it.

Thanks to Snir, I realized what I am proposing here is very parallel to https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/FunLike/IsApply.html

So most of the considerations that went into the design of these classes likely applies here as well.
Seeing that this design appears elsewhere in Mathlib does persuade me into thinking this might be a good idea after all. I apologize for my earlier skepticism.

Just fyi: the Is*Apply classes are not used anywhere yet - there is a PR for ContinuousLinearMap and I will do more once that has been merged.
The reason I want to have them (besides the obvious point that it forces the library to be more consistent and it is easier to catch missing instances, etc) is that there are cases where I want to prove things about a function space. We have the support of a distribution (a continuous linear map) docs#Distribution.dsupport, but we can't say that the support of the sum of two distributions is contained in the union of the supports, because we would need to specialize to a specific class of distributions, but they are all different type synonyms of ContinuousLinearMap with different topologies. So without IsAddApply we would need one lemma per class of distribution, which is very silly and not very mathlib appropriate.
As a more trivial example, we have several versions of the sum_apply lemma, but we do not have it in every case where it is true.
Another application (IsConcreteCsSup): #mathlib4 > Zorn's lemma for constructing morphisms

As @Martin Winter says, there's probably a better design idea hiding here. The status quo of thousands of lines of copy-pasted code is a big concern to me, but I'm not sure having 20 different IsConcrete classes is the best idea either.

In all cases, the thing we want is "operation X on SubFoos corresponds to the same operation on sets." We could have a generic typeclass IsConcrete operation which means something like "SetLike.coe (operation arg) = operation (SetLike.coe arg), where operation comes from a notation typeclass? This definition would need to be general enough to take arbitrary arguments depending on the types in the SetLike A B instance.

Artie Khovanov said:

I'm not sure having 20 different IsConcrete classes is the best idea either

We have lots of Is*Apply classes (15?), why not IsConcrete* classes as well? (if they're useful)
That's fair. It's certainly a lighter-weight design and won't have that much code duplication.

btw Sets don't have IsConcreteLE so lattice lemmas that rely on it currently have to be duplicated.
Could we either make Sets SetLike, or spell IsConcreteLE using Membership instead of SetLike?
I was also wondered why Set is not SetLike :thinking: (and functions are not FunLike).
I'm fine with this level of duplication. I think we should focus on reducing duplication between different SubFoos before we worry about a universal solution.
#42661 - concreteness typeclasses for lattice operations

Snir Broshi said:

btw Sets don't have IsConcreteLE so lattice lemmas that rely on it currently have to be duplicated.
Could we either make Sets SetLike, or spell IsConcreteLE using Membership instead of SetLike?

#42666 - generalise docs#IsConcreteLE to docs#Membership
Do we have a reason to believe that generalizing to Membership is a better solution than making Sets SetLike? It might well be the better solution, but I'm not sure.
you would then get a setlike coercion from sets to sets
SetLike requires an injective coercion, but some structures have a non-injective one, e.g. List / Multiset
Multisets don't satisfy IsConcreteLE, but they do satisfy docs#Multiset.mem_inter and docs#Multiset.mem_union for example, and they can never be SetLike
I think we should make this generalisation anyway. I've been convinced by the Multiset example. As Snir says, they have a concrete preorder, sup, and inf.
Separately, I fear making sets SetLike would lead to issues with coercions and typeclass inference -- it feels like a bad instance -- but I don't know enough about that.
The order on Multiset is not the order that is concrete, right? But indeed it does have lawful sup/inf/bot. So probably those classes should be generalized to Membership in #42661.

Can we think about the naming again before introducing more of it? I don't find the Concrete-names particularly intuitive.

Before Snir's request to generalize I would have suggested SetLikeLE etc. This seems off the table. What about LawfulLE following Jovan's use of the term? Or perhaps SetLE to reflect the relation to set?
Could HasConcreteLE instead of IsConcreteLE be more gramatical?

The noncomputable and Classical.choice in #42661 seem avoidable if we just turn around how we intend to use the concrete classes. Here is an example from our polyhedral repo:

instance : Bot (Polytope R X) where
  bot := ⟨∅, IsPolytope.empty R X⟩

instance : IsConcreteBot (Polytope R X) X := ⟨rfl⟩

instance : OrderBot (Polytope R X) := .ofSetLike ..

Would it be so bad to let this be the intended use?

Another question: What about conditionally complete lattices? Their sSup isn't concrete/lawful, but IsLUB is. Should we add a separate class for IsLUB, or will it make the sSup class redundant and we should just use IsLUB? Or add a BddAbove assumption to the sSup class?

I'm not sure about examples in Mathlib, but e.g.

-- the intuitive `SupSet` on `Finset`s isn't concrete/lawful
open scoped Classical in
noncomputable instance : SupSet (Finset ℕ) where
  sSup s := if h : s.Finite then h.toFinset.biUnion id else ∅

-- using von Neumann ordinals (each number is the set of numbers below it),
-- the existing `SupSet ℕ` isn't concrete/lawful
instance : SetLike ℕ ℕ where
  coe := Set.Iio
  coe_injective := Set.Iio_injective
I would call it IsConcreteCSSup and yes I think we want this

Martin Winter said:

The noncomputable and Classical.choice in #42661 seem avoidable if we just turn around how we intend to use the concrete classes.

I want to have the option to create the data, just like with PartialOrder.ofSetLike. You can always fix defeqs with spread notation! I think my current design allows both things?

hmm
maybe Iff.rfl could be the default proof of the field in IsConcreteFoo?
that would support your pattern

Martin Winter said:

Can we think about the naming again before introducing more of it? I don't find the Concrete-names particularly intuitive.

Sure, idrm the name. We could call it eg MembershipFoo: MembershipSup, MembershipInf, etc
Or just MemSup MemInf like we have eg ZeroAdd

Artie Khovanov said:

Or just MemSup MemInf like we have eg ZeroAdd

This is my favorite so far. If we expect confusion with a class that expresses membership (which would also start with Mem...), we could use IsMemFoo or HasMemFoo.
We should use Is anyway because it's a Prop
So IsConcreteLE -> IsMemLE

#42702 - renames
IsConcreteLE -> IsMemLE
LE.ofSetLike -> LE.ofMembership
SetLike.le_def -> Membership.le_def, etc (for theorems that don't need SetLike)
thoughts? (I haven't made the renames outside the file yet because I'm not sure about the last one especially)
